rationale: El Guerrouj's 3:43.13 has stood since 1999 and remains one of the toughest records; Kerr (PB 3:45.34) has openly built his whole 2026 season around Project 222 in London but has not raced a mile/1500 all year, so breakthrough is a real but <50% shot.

Dos Santos is unbeaten in 2026 (WL 46.72 Xiamen, 46.89 Oslo) and has beaten Warholm three times head-to-head; Warholm (46.82) is the home-crowd-adjacent record holder who won Silesia 2025 in 46.28 and remains the main threat.

Confirmed Silesia duel: 2026 rankings #1 Jefferson-Wooden (WL 10.84 Stockholm, defends her 2025 Silesia title) vs #2 Alfred (10.76 Oslo); very close but Jefferson-Wooden has the edge and beat Alfred 3-1 in 2025.

2026 Sydney elite field not yet published; organisers publicly courted Sawe/Kejelcha/Kiplimo but they are more likely pointed at Berlin/Chicago after London sub-2hrs; recent Sydney winners are Ethiopian-heavy (Kiros CR 2:06:06 in 2025, Gobena 2nd); hilly course levelers the field.

No 2026 field published; Hassan set the CR (2:18:22) and Kosgei was 2nd in 2025 and both raced Sydney last year, but the Abbott Majors rotation and fall majors make Hassan's return uncertain; top Ethiopian marathoners (Edesa, Amebaw 1:05:07 HM, Zeray 1:05:12 HM) are plausible new faces.

Ingebrigtsen (Olympic champ, auto-qualified) and Hocker (world champ, auto-qualified) headline; Ingebrigtsen has been quiet in 2026 while Hocker/Yihune (WL 12:47.62 Oslo) are in-form, so a modest edge despite being the marquee name.

Yan (17) threw a massive WL 71.74 Xiamen; world champion Angulo (auto-qualified) and rankings #1 Vilagos are contenders; Kitaguchi is defending Olympic champ and 2025 worlds medallist but only 62.86 this year.
Pathirage leads 2026 (92.62 Rome WL, 88.68 Doha win); Peters 2nd in both, ranking #1 Weber, 2025 world champ Walcott and returning Chopra (85.69 Doha) all auto-qualified/invited; throws are volatile.
Lyles is reigning world/Olympic-invited champion and 2026 rankings #1 (19.91 in April opener); Tebogo 19.96 Rabat behind Bednarek 19.69; Gout Gout (19.67 April) will need to be at peak in September.

Award due Sept 2026 at Council; London has govt support and a strong bid but West Ham stadium access in September is a reported blocker; Nairobi has a strong bid and Coe backs Africa hosting (with election politics to consider); Rome has govt support, Munich prefers 2031.

Chemnung has 2026 WL 1:04:01 (Barcelona) and is focused on fall marathon training (Chicago), so a Copenhagen HM start is uncertain; Taye 1:04:22 Riga is the top Ethiopian road threat, with Gebreselama, Belayneh and Amebaw close behind.
